news.title: Diego Maradona’s infamous ‘Hand of God’ FIFA World Cup 1986 ball sells for millions at auction
news.lede: The football used when Diego Maradona scored his famous ‘Hand of God’ goal against England at the 1986 World Cup has sold for £2.5m at auction. The Adidas Azteca ball was sold for $3.3m at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday.Maradona used his hand to punch the ball past England goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina’s 2-1 quarter-final win. He later described the goal as being scored “a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God”. The ball was kept by match referee Ali Bin Nasser for more than three decades.Diego Maradona’s ball was part of one of football’s most famous matchesThe auction price was below expectations.

news.title: FIFA unveils 2027 Women's World Cup schedule as Brazil prepares for iconic Maracana final
news.lede: Football's global governing body has confirmed the full 64-match schedule for the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil. The legendary Maracana in Rio de Janeiro will take centre stage, hosting both the opening fixture and the grand finale. All eight host cities across the vibrant South American nation are set to welcome knockout-stage football as anticipation builds for the historic tournament. FIFA unveiled the complete 64-game fixture list on August 20 at their Zurich headquarters.

news.title: Rodri capture can catapult Barcelona back to very top of European game: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer window
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: Diego Maradona's iconic 1986 'Hand of God' World Cup ball sells for $3.35m at auction
news.lede: Bidding opened at $2.5 million on the night of the event before reaching its final hammer price. The publication also noted that the final sum fell short of the all-time record for a sports ball, which remains held by baseball star Shohei Ohtani's 50th home run ball after it commanded $4.392 million in 2024. Timing dampens bidding interestThe artefact previously changed hands for $2.37 million at Graham Budd Auctions in 2022 before failing to sell the following year when a top bid of $2.04 million did not meet the reserve price. Its relisting this summer sought to capitalise on the excitement surrounding the 2026 World Cup.

news.title: ‘Doesn’t have the support’: FIFA boss put on notice as stunning leadership challenge looms
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been delivered a stunning warning over his future, with UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin declaring he must recognise he has lost the support of the football world or prepare to face a leadership challenge. Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his controversial and now-abandoned proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup. Get all the latest football news, highlights and analysis delivered straight to your inbox with Fox Sports Sportmail. The saga has created an extraordinary divide within world football, with UEFA threatening a boycott of FIFA competitions and several continental and national federations withdrawing their support for the 56-year-old.

news.title: Ceferin rules out Fifa presidency - who are the candidates who could run against Infantino?
news.lede: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out of the running for the Fifa presidency but said Gianni Infantino would probably face a challenger if he seeks re-election next year following a global backlash over a plan to sell part of the World Cup to private investors. Speaking to The Rest Is Politics: Leading podcast, which ​will air on Monday, Ceferin said he was not interested in succeeding Infantino despite growing uncertainty around the Fifa ⁠president's future. "My credibility is much, much, much ​higher if ⁠I'm not interested in the position," Ceferin said. Ceferin criticised the proposed World Cup investment project, describing it as a greater threat to the sport than the European Super League plan that Uefa successfully fought in 2021.

news.title: Infantino announces launch of Under-15 World Cup with 211 teams taking part
news.lede: "It will be like a festival for children". Gianni Infantino has confirmed that the International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) will organise the first-ever Under-15 World Cup this year, open to all 211 member associations. Talk of the project had been swirling in recent weeks. Now the FIFA president has publicly committed to making it happen.

news.title: CommBank Junior Matildas Gear Up for U-17 World Cup
news.lede: The CommBank Junior Matildas will assemble for their final domestic training camp ahead of FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026™, with Australia's debut in the tournament set to kick off on October 19th against Chile. CommBank Junior Matildas Head Coach, Michael Cooper, has called in a 28-player squad for the upcoming training camp, as his coaching staff have their final opportunity to make selection choices ahead of the squad announcement for the upcoming FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026™. Australia qualified for the first-ever time for the showpiece U-17 event following the team's fourth-place finish at the AFC U-17 Women's Asian Cup 2026™, with the tournament set to provide invaluable experience for Australia's next generation of stars.
